Vesper tucks the key safely into her satchel and drops her voice to a whisper. "Thank you for the quiet, big fellow, I'll try not to wake you." She wades into the Keepers' gallery, keeping the lamp's gold at her back, and follows the river air up toward the Water-Stair to catch Odalie and find the Reeve before Ashgrove thinks to circle the hill.

"DM: when I get out, can I still hear the bell in town, and is Brannoc Vell's watch answering it yet?"

entries.text: dice Vesper's Perception (hearing) for the town's response from the gallery's far end, DC 10: 1d20+1 = 1d20 [12] + 1 = 13

The gallery is a cold, ankle-deep crawl. The roof presses low enough that you stoop, and the lamp's gold fades behind you until your darkvision turns everything to grey. After a long, dripping climb you reach the landing under the carved lantern arch, the same one you passed on the way in, and the Water-Stair opens beneath you toward the river.

The town's answer reaches you there, and it's good news. The bell you rang has been taken up. Below the hill, other bells are tolling, a ragged chorus from the Grand Quay, the tannery chapel and the fish-market. Over them you hear a deeper sound, a war-horn of the kind the Harbour Reeve's watch blows when the river is in flood. Shouting rolls up the hill road, and boots with it. Torches bob at the foot of the slope. The watch is answering, and by the sound of it, so are a good many townsfolk who've spent two days behind shutters.

Above you, muffled by stone, Ashgrove's men are shouting orders now rather than waiting. The polite voice is gone.

The hooded cloak is still on your back, and the Disguise Self still wears Odalie's face. A few steps down, a lantern glows at the foot of the stair, with Old Mags's stooped silhouette beside it, waving you on.

One note, as your DM: your sheet's status now shows you at 2nd level, with 15 maximum hit points, three spell slots, a Garrow Quill's half of a sluice-pin I haven't introduced, and no rapier listed. I'll treat the sheet as the record. If any of that is a surprise, tell me and we'll sort it out.

Your rapier is missing from the item list, and there's an item called "Garrow Quill's half of the sluice-pin" that never came up in our story. Your level and XP also read differently from what I'd tracked. I won't invent a history for any of it. If you have context for these, tell me and I'll fold it in. For now I'm treating the sheet as the truth, so you have no rapier on you.

The Keepers' gallery slopes up through cold, ankle-deep water, and the lamp's gold fades behind you until your darkvision is all there is. The ceiling is low enough to make you stoop. The floor is worn into a shallow trough by feet from long before the town existed. The river air gets stronger, and you hear the slow drip of the Water-Stair somewhere ahead.

About a hundred paces on, the gallery meets the stair at the landing under the carved lantern arch. The bell has stopped. You rang it until you left, so the town has had nothing more from it, but the echo of it hangs over the roofs. Farther off, thin and flat, is the note of a watch horn, blown twice, and then a long pause.

Whether that is Brannoc Vell or Sorrel Thack, you can't tell yet. Nobody is on the stair. Above you through the grate is the cellar, where your two bound raiders lie. Below you the stair runs down toward Eel Row and Old Mags, where Odalie should be, if she made it.

The gallery lets you out at the landing under the carved lantern arch, on the Water-Stair you climbed an hour ago. The grate you forced hangs open below you. The two bound raiders are gone from the cellar. Only a scatter of dice and a cut length of Mags's cord are left.

A few things on your sheet don't match what I narrated: it shows you at level 2 with more hit points, your rapier gone, and a "sluice-pin" half belonging to a Garrow Quill that I have no record of. Tell me what happened with those, or tell me to go on and I'll treat the sheet as true.

For now, the stair runs down toward Eel Row, and Odalie with it. Above you, the sanctuary, the ram and Ashgrove are still within reach.

line:
Vesper lets the disguise drop with a rueful laugh, raises both hands, and steps lightly onto the barrels as if she'd planned it. "Well, Captain, you've caught me being predictable. A kettle is the first honest thing anyone's offered me tonight, and I'd hate to waste it."

She keeps her tail tucked and her eyes on the cabin door while she signals Ysolt with two slow fingers down by her hip: *wait.* "Mind if I bring my own cup? I'd like to hear what a woman with half the words offers for the other half."

entries.text:
Before the scene moves, a note from the DM. Your sheet now lists a second-level bard (HP 13/15, 3 slots, no rapier), a "Brass lantern key" and "Garrow Quill's half of the sluice-pin". None of those happened in our story so far, since Ashgrove took the key and the satchel. I'm not going to build on them until we settle what they are, so tell me if they're yours. For now I'll treat the key as Ashgrove's and the sheet as having a glitch.

The disguise slides off you like wet paint, and the sentry's crossbow follows every move. You step up onto the barrels with your hands wide. Out in the reeds, Ysolt's dark shape goes still at your two-finger signal and doesn't loose.

Ashgrove laughs, a real laugh, quiet and delighted. "Bring your own cup, by all means. I admire a guest who negotiates the tea." She stands aside from the cabin door. Inside, a lamp swings over a plank table with a kettle, two chipped cups and your satchel, its flap open. The brass key lies beside it, gleaming in the lamplight. Four raiders sit along the walls with crossbows across their knees, watching you, and the sentry's bolt stays pointed at the small of your back.

"Sit," she says. "You have something I need, and it isn't in your pockets, and I have something you need, and it is in plain view. Let's be civilized about the trade. Corvin's choir will go on singing for a while. I'd rather like to hear you try to talk me out of it."

Behind her the cabin's far wall is a rotted shutter, and under your feet the deck is soft with damp. Your spell slots are spent, but you have three Bardic Inspiration dice in reserve and a lot of nerve.

entries.text:
Ashgrove's smile widens by a fraction. "A cup of her own. Of course. Dessa, a second cup."

The sentry's crossbow follows you up the gangplank without wavering, and the two men on deck fall in behind you. Your signal to Ysolt is a small thing and nobody sees it. Out in the reeds a dark shape goes still.

The cabin is warmer than it has any right to be. It's a low, tarred room with a brazier, a map table and two stools, and it smells of tea and lamp-oil. Your satchel sits on the table with its flap open, and Ashgrove lowers herself onto a stool across from it with her white glove resting on the wood. A brass lantern-key lies beside the cup, polished and catching the light. She pours without hurry.

"Half the words," she says. "You're quick, Miss Thorne. I'd wondered who would come: the old woman, or the girl she hid it with. I confess I hoped for you." She slides a cup across. "Here is what I offer. You say the Keepers' words with me at the new moon, and the Sleeper is mine. Marrowmere pays a fair tribute, and you and your Sister live comfortably at the top of the hill, and every river-town between here and the sea learns your name. Or I take them from the old woman, and I won't be polite about it."

Outside, the song from the *Plump Heron* is drifting closer. Her men are crowding the cabin door, listening and watching. The tea steams between you.

A DM note: your sheet now reads differently than I had it. It shows you at 13 of 15 hit points with a brass lantern key in your own pack, so I'm running from it as it stands.

line:
Vesper lets the disguise drop with a rueful laugh, raises both hands, and steps lightly onto the barrels as if she'd planned it. "Well, Captain, you've caught me being predictable. A kettle is the first honest thing anyone's offered me tonight, and I'd hate to waste it."

She keeps her tail tucked and her eyes on the cabin door while she signals Ysolt with two slow fingers down by her hip: *wait.* "Mind if I bring my own cup? I'd like to hear what a woman with half the words offers for the other half."

entries.text:
The disguise slides off you like a dropped coat, and your hands go up. Down by your hip, two slow fingers say *wait*. Out in the black reeds, the dark shape that is Ysolt Pike holds very still.

Ashgrove laughs, a short, real laugh, the first you've heard from her. "Oh, I do like you. Bring your cup, by all means. Garrick, search her. Gently."

The scarred sentry pats you down with the care of a man who dislikes his job. He takes your dagger and tosses it onto the deck. He finds the silver bowl under your coat and weighs it, then hands it back with a baffled grunt. Then you're walking up the gangplank between two crossbows, onto a deck that smells of tar and wet rope. The cabin door is open to lamplight.

Inside it's almost cozy. There's a small table, a kettle on a brazier and two tin cups, and Odalie's green-waxed satchel sits open between them with its flap folded back. Ashgrove sits with her white-gloved hand around a cup. She nods you to the other stool.

"Half the words," she says warmly. "Yes. Thack was quite thorough. Here is my offer, Miss Thorne. Give me the Keepers' words, and nobody is hurt, not your Sister, not your Reeve, not that dreadful little town. I'll even pay. Fifty gold now, a ship's share after. Refuse, and a boat is already on its way to Eel Row, with instructions to ask Odalie politely."

Through the cabin wall, the drunken chorus on the river is still singing. The sentry's crossbow sits at your back.

A note out of character: your sheet now shows things I never gave you: a brass lantern key, "Garrow Quill's half of the sluice-pin," level-2 stats, and no rapier. I'll treat the sheet as the record, but I'd like to know where you think those came from before I build on them.

Level up! New spell: Healing Word, since I've nearly died once already and a heal at range beats a prayer. No swaps, and I'll take the fixed 6 hit points, because I don't trust my luck with a d8 after that natural 1 at the hulk.

Then she holds up the key to the lantern light. "Corvin, drop us at Tanner's Stair by dawn. Ashgrove means to open the Weeping Locks at the new moon and drown the lower town, so I need Odalie, the Reeve, and a way to break that lock before then."

entries.text:
Before you pick anything, I checked the sheet, and the level-up isn't pending.

The sheet shows you're already a 2nd-level bard. You have 15 maximum hit points (13 now), three 1st-level slots (all spent), and 2 hit dice. Healing Word is already among your spells known, so there's no new spell to take and nothing to swap. Your XP reads 425, and 3rd level needs 900. I called it "300 XP, level 2" in my last message, and that was wrong. Nothing needs recording, and your good instincts about Healing Word stand.

Two other things on the sheet:

- Your rapier is gone, because the sentry took it off the barrel on the hulk. You still have the dagger, which is a poor trade.
- You have an item called "Garrow Quill's half of the sluice-pin" that I don't remember giving you. Tell me where you picked it up and who Garrow Quill is, and I'll fold it into the story rather than guess.

For the story: Corvin nods at the tiller and the *Plump Heron* turns upriver for Tanner's Stair, with Ysolt dozing against a bale and the key warm in your fist. You should reach the stair near dawn and have the day to work with. Six nights remain before the new moon, with the Weeping Locks to break or guard and Ashgrove still out there.
